The main takeaway from our work is that

, under a natural assumption of diminishing returns to information, the principal can coordinate the agents' exploration-exploitation trade-off by recommending a single alternative at every time-step, without the need to know the agents' types or the underlying environment.

, in the Bayesian setting, the principal can achieve this goal by using a very simple randomized recommendation policy, and the agents' incentives can be fully aligned with the principal's objective, even when they are myopic.
